sections.overview: Parascyllium ferrugineum, the Rusty Carpetshark, is an Australian carpetshark in the family Parascylliidae, found along southern coasts.
sections.identification: It has brown, rust-coloured saddles or spots along the body and fins. It may reach about 80 cm in total length.
sections.habitat: It occurs from Western Australia east to Victoria and Tasmania, near rocky reefs, river mouths, seagrass and algal beds, and in offshore waters.
sections.diet: It feeds on bottom-dwelling crustaceans and molluscs.
sections.behavior: Individuals may shelter in caves or beneath rocky ledges during the day. The species is occasionally discarded as trawl or Danish-seine bycatch.
sections.reproduction: In summer, females lay yellow egg cases with long tendrils; pups are about 17 cm long at birth.
sections.ecology: Its close relative, the Collar Carpetshark, Parascyllium collare, is concentrated farther east and has a conspicuous dark neck band. The Rusty Carpetshark ranges farther west and bears rusty-brown saddles.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN category of Least Concern. Bycatch is recorded, but the consulted sources do not establish a population trend.
